Triggers.value: Night-time or waking up in the dark
A specific texture associated with the event

Maladaptive Strategies.value: give up important responsibilities to stay safe or avoid triggers
I drift off into a world of my own
make sure never to be alone with another person

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
I feel like an object, not like a person
You can never know who will harm you

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

issues.item: Threat: missing/none selected despite multiple current-danger and exposure-related items
issues.explanation: The profile contains several items implying an active sense of present threat or exposure (e.g., 'World is Dangerous', 'Exposed to Others', concealment to avoid being noticed), yet the Threat component is entirely absent. For this trauma type, such items would usually cohere with at least some explicit threat content; the omission makes the cross-node picture clinically uneven.

'World is Dangerous' expresses a broad ongoing threat belief, but the formulation specifies no active links into or out of Threat and no Threat items are endorsed. This makes the appraisal sit awkwardly in the formulation because it functions more like a threat belief than an isolated negative self-appraisal.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Concealing Clothing: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed
issues.explanation: 'Concealing Clothing ... to avoid being noticed' implies active management of current interpersonal threat/visibility. With Threat completely unrepresented and no Trigger→Threat or Maladaptive Strategies→Threat linkage in the formulation, this strategy lacks a clear matching symptom target in the rest of the profile.

Threat: missing/none selected despite multiple current-danger and exposure-related items

issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: The Threat node is not clinically coherent here. 'Flashbacks' and 'Physical Reactivity' are re-experiencing/arousal responses rather than threat appraisals, while the only genuine threat appraisal selected is 'Threat from Strangers.' That mixes different constructs within one node.

vignette: Mark, a 25-year-old North American male, has been struggling with the aftermath of childhood physical abuse inflicted by his caregiver. Mark's life has become a series of coping mechanisms and avoidance strategies that have gradually eroded his sense of self and security. The traumatic event occurred during his childhood when he was frequently subjected to severe beatings in a dark room. The texture of the carpet where these incidents took place continues to be a potent trigger for him, particularly in settings where similar textures are present. Nighttime has also become deeply unsettling; Mark wakes up repeatedly in the dark with a sense of dread and overwhelming fear. These triggers have significantly impacted Mark's life as a housekeeper. The tactile reminders, combined with the auditory cues such as children crying, create intense distress that he struggles to manage. He often drops his responsibilities or avoids certain tasks to stay safe from these triggers, leading him to drift off into a world of his own where he feels more in control. Mark's memories of those painful experiences are vivid and overwhelming. When triggered, the memory replays like a film, reliving every detail through all senses simultaneously, leaving him feeling completely overwhelmed by emotion. This replaying of memories often leads him to drop responsibilities further, as he finds it nearly impossible to continue his work when such intense flashbacks occur. His negative appraisals stem from these traumatic experiences; Mark feels that others can see the abuse etched into his very being, making him feel dehumanized and objectified. This belief intensifies his fear of harm, as he believes anyone could potentially cause more damage. These thoughts fuel his triggers further, creating a cycle where he constantly monitors for signs of danger. The physical reactivity to these memories exacerbates Mark's hypervigilance, making him superalert and watchful at all times. This constant state of alertness has led him to ensure that he is never alone, always seeking the presence of others as a form of protection. However, this need for company also stems from his fear of being vulnerable again. Mark's maladaptive strategies have evolved over time in response to these triggers and memories. When triggered by nighttime or dark environments, he retreats into fantasy escapes where he feels more secure. The overwhelming nature of the memory often leads him back to dropping responsibilities, as he finds it nearly impossible to function while reliving such traumatic experiences. The cycle becomes increasingly self-reinforcing: his maladaptive strategies, like drifting off into a world of his own and ensuring he is never alone, have inadvertently prolonged the memories and negative appraisals. The fantasy escapes provide temporary relief but do little to address the underlying trauma, which continues to be triggered by similar environments and sensory cues. Mark's current state reflects weeks and months of this pattern forming habits that have significantly impacted how he lives and works. His occupation as a housekeeper has become increasingly challenging due to these avoidance behaviors, leading to strained relationships with his colleagues and employers. The consequences are clear: Mark is no longer able to fulfill his responsibilities effectively. What finally brought him to seek help was the realization that his life had been significantly compromised by this unending cycle of triggers, memories, and maladaptive strategies. He is most afraid of being completely consumed by these experiences but also most hopeful for a future where he can reclaim his sense of self and live without constant fear.
